title: THE HIGHWAY OF THE UPRIGHT: AN ISRAELITES'S STRAIT JOURNEY

sense.text:
“The highway of the upright” is the title of the class: the highway of the upright, an Israelite’s strait journey. Strait not as in a straight line, though we do walk a straight line, but strait as in hard, difficult, challenging to walk.

“The highway of the upright is to depart from evil.” To depart from evil, the upright have to know what evil is. Evil is sin, and sin is the breaking of God’s commandments. So we are constantly walking a road where evil comes up before us, and we have to stay upright on that evil road. It is like a video game: as we go down the path, evil comes up. The lust to show myself, the lust to eat what I want, the lust to do whatever I please.

The upright is the man that keeps the commandments. Going down the strait path, you walk the upright path. If you are wicked as hell, you are walking the wide path: you have no accountability, and no one can tell you what to do. That is why eighty percent of black women are overweight, and forty-nine or fifty percent are obese, and that was not the case in 1970 and before. Take the black man out of the household, and not only does he put his children through things, like Joe Jackson did, but he puts his wife through things too: no, you’re not eating that. The whole order has been broken up, and it has been systematic.

“He that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.” His way, if we are men of God and women of God, is God’s way. We are going to fall and we are going to make mistakes. But despite being in captivity, despite single-parent households, divorce rates at an all-time high, economic confusion in our community and unsuccessful marriages, we still have to walk in these commandments. That is the Israelite’s strait journey, and keeping the commandments through all of it is actually our strength.

precepts.why:
Christ says, “Enter ye in at the strait gate.” The strait gate is not a gate with perfect ninety-degree angles, linearly straight. Strait means challenging, difficult, full of obstacles. That is the highway of the upright.

“For wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction.” Wide and broad is easy on people. A wide, broad way lets you go over here and over there; it gives you what they call liberty, liberty and freedom of choice. And God has never been about freedom of choice with us. “And many there be which go in thereat”: that is not the strait gate. That is the wide, easy gate, full of options, full of liberty, full of choices.

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way”: narrow means it is specific, it is conditional. That is why Christ said, If ye love me, keep my commandments. There have always been conditions with the Most High God and his Son. That narrow way is the one “which leadeth unto life”, eternal life, “and few there be that find it.”

So the highway of the upright is the strait gate and the narrow way. The wicked go in at the wide gate with no accountability; the upright walk the narrow way, keeping the commandments, and that is the way that preserves the soul.

“My son, forget not my law.” When we forget God’s laws, the nuclear family of the Israelites gets destroyed: it uncouples. A couple is a connection, like railroad cars coupled to one another. You can’t have a train without the cars coupled together; break them apart and the train goes off the track. Picture a train with many cars riding down the tracks, and the head car, which is the husband, gets uncoupled. That is what they have done to the black community, and since about the mid to late sixties every stat has gone downhill morally. As the twelve tribes of Israel, when you destroy the marriages, you have uncoupled the entire nation. And when I say black America, that is the whole nation: the Puerto Ricans, Dominicans and Cubans who came to this country after Judah paved the way, and those in Central America who have not yet got their wake-up call.

“But let thine heart keep my commandments.” When we keep the commandments of God, that is how we don’t forget his law. The law is the commandments.

“For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.” That is why black men have the shortest lifespan of any category: we live very stressful lives because we don’t have successful marriages, and we die prematurely. The number one killer of black men in this country is heart disease, and a lot of that we can control. We are not even keeping the laws on how to eat. When the Israelites forgot God’s laws, we got shorter days, no peace in our marriages and no peace in our households.

The numbers show it: non-Hispanic black adults have the highest first divorce rates, black men the highest among men and black women the highest of all, and black women initiate divorce at the highest rate. All of it skyrocketed after 1970, when Roe versus Wade legalized the abortion of children. Yet from Emancipation through Reconstruction, the black codes and Jim Crow, with all that overt and covert racism and hard times, we had much higher morals and standards of marriage. The pictures of black couples from 1900 to 1970 show it: the men in their position as the head, the women in dresses and not obese, an order of God. It is a damn shame what it has become.

On the highway of the upright, the sisters have a role in rebuilding our nation, and it is not the dominant role. “And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” From the beginning the woman was meet, agreeable, to help the man. That was always her role: the black woman is a support mate to her Israelite husband.

A sister who is waiting for a husband has to fast and pray that the Most High send her a husband, and do the things she needs to do to prepare. That is her trial. Bishop Nathanyel taught the three trials of faith years ago: the personal trials and the marital trials. For a single brother or sister waiting to be married, the waiting and the celibacy are the beginning of the marital trial.

When you remove the breadwinner from the house, the woman no longer has the role of a help. Now she has to be the breadwinner, which by default comes with a masculine set of standards. The breadwinner is more than the one who picks up bread from the grocery store: he is the provider, working, maintaining and protecting, the first to the door to stop the thief. Take one father out of a neighborhood and the other fathers can make up the difference; take ninety percent of the fathers out and you have crippled the entire people. When the mother is forced to be both breadwinner and emotional support, the emotional support goes wanting, and the children suffer depression.

A woman can help develop certain qualities in a man, compassion toward women and empathy, but she is not qualified to produce a man. A man teaches a young man how to deal with stress and go through things. A black mother got honest that her own son told her at seventeen: if you really loved me, you would have taught me how to survive the things you were afraid of, instead of only protecting me. Mothers cuddle them and become a wall of security that comes crashing down when they are eighteen and nineteen and sent out into the world unprotected.

On the highway of the upright we walk the strait path, not the wide gate with all its choices and freedoms, and evil is constantly coming at us. Bishop Nathanyel once showed a cartoon of a race: the black runner starts five laps behind and has to go over potholes and jump hurdles, while the others have a head start and run with no obstacles. Even so, we are required to keep the commandments, with all these things coming at us that make it even harder. If we do not have God’s laws, there is no hope at all for black people. However much riches you get, you have a destroyed psyche.

“And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee”: you Israelites, men, women and children. “But to fear the Lord thy God.” We are supposed to be afraid of our Daddy. That is the importance of the black man in the house: there is only so much you will do when you know Dad is going to hold you accountable. Take the black man out of the house, and by twelve, thirteen or fourteen that boy no longer respects his mother’s authority, however strong she is. In the same way, we did not respect God’s authority, and as a result he allowed the nations to chastise us.

“To walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the Lord thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul.” Walking in God’s ways is keeping the commandments, doing it and doing it over and over again, on a highway that is filled with evil, strait and hard to deal with.

Forty years ago, in 1986, a room of black teenage mothers laughed when one of them said she would like to marry her baby’s father, and she hung her head; the rest said they didn’t want a man holding them down. That was only twenty years after the civil rights movement, and that is how far we fell. It is a direct result of slavery, of our disobedience, of Willie Lynch. Married couples don’t abort children, and there have been over nineteen million abortions among black women since 1970.

That is why Joe Jackson made his boys carry bricks from one end of the yard to the other: to keep them out of the streets and out of trouble, and to make them tough. Black boys need structure; they need to go through some goddamn pain. Take that out of the household and you produce angry, emotional boys who never became men. Some of you black men are weak as hell, and among us it is going to become taboo to be fat.

Peter speaks of the fiery trials on our highway to the kingdom. “Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you.” The institutional racism, the violent crimes from organizations like the KKK, police brutality: all of that is still going to be there. But how much easier it is to fight spiritually when your family unit is intact. The fiery trial is to try you and to try me.

“As though some strange thing happened unto you”: don’t be surprised. Many of us in our thirties, forties and fifties come from broken households, parents divorced, a father who bounced or was never there. Without a father we did not get the emotional intelligence to process things as they come our way, so men make terrible decisions and get angry quick without thinking logically, and many become emotional eaters. Children raised in a two-parent household, with the father at the lead and the mother supporting him, get that balance: the father keeps the little girl balancing on the wobbly tray, ready to catch her if she falls but not letting her give up, and she learns not to cry and quit.

That is why the marriages in this truth are so important: we are stopping the cycle that happened to most of us. Christ and Paul kept saying, walk in my ways; God kept saying, walk in my ways, keep my commandments. The fiery trial is the trial of the upright on that highway, and the upright is the man that keeps the commandments.

A lot of you men who are overweight and obese are emotional, because most of you were raised by your mothers and never went through anything real to get that weak, sorry, yellow, make-me-sad spirit off you. There ought to be a brick retreat, moving stuff all across the yard for a month straight, to get all that weakness out of you.

The marriage rate among us is twenty-three percent, so the divorce rate is the inverse, seventy-seven; seventy-one percent of our women are not married and twenty-nine percent never will be, and thirty-four percent of black men have decided they will never get married. Black men who marry outside don’t really want the other nations; deep down they want the submissiveness and the quiet spirit they see. That is why what we are doing is revolutionary: you cannot build a nation and teach them to get to the kingdom unless you fix the nucleus of the household. Among us every metric of society is supposed to be the opposite: a hundred percent marriage rate, no divorce (if there are big problems, separate and follow the scriptures), no single-parent households. And with group economics there should be no poor amongst us, brothers buying the parts and donating the labor to fix each other’s cars, just as we have done with the land.

sense.text:
The order of God has been the same since the time of Adam and Eve: Eve was designed and made for Adam as an help meet for him. This is the divine order of God. “But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ”: Christ is the head of the Israelite man. “And the head of the woman is the man.”

When our people have successful marriages, or even just stay together and don’t divorce, they produce emotionally sound children that can deal with life. Now give that same man and woman Christ and the word of God, and everything changes. That is why they want to stop us from teaching the laws, statutes and commandments and the faith of Christ, that we are Israel. Islam didn’t work, and Christianity is the foundation of the eighty percent of children raised in single-parent households.

When the woman is the breadwinner, she raises children who may be strong in some ways but can’t stay on task and go through challenges. All the Jacksons were successful because of Joe. Before 1965, even in the Christian church, our people held more morals: divorce was forbidden, women wore dresses and conservative clothing and carried their books in front of their breasts, a young man knocked at the door and asked the father before taking his daughter out, and chaperones and double dating come from our culture. Then came the civil rights era and the civil liberties.

Black men teach boys to stand in the face of damn opposition. In 1968 a black teacher told a four-year-old he was six, and kept pressing until the boy stood up and said his true age; you shouldn’t be weak, you stand up and say it. That is how we have to stand on principle when it comes to marriage: come, get married, be honorable, and if you have problems, work through them.

The father represents the law in the home. A black married sister said in 1968 that the black man doesn’t want his wife punching a time card alongside him; he wants her home, just like the white man wants his wife home. When a child is hurt he goes to mama, but when he has a problem he goes to daddy, because daddy is the symbol of law. With the father as the law and the mother at home, you eliminate illegitimate pregnancies.

In 1986 a sister said society had made living without a husband easy: welfare is not the best thing for everybody, teenage pregnancy cannot be stopped by programs, it has to be morals, and morals come from God. When she was a girl it was not morally acceptable to have babies without a husband. If Martin Luther King were alive, she said, he would be talking about the destruction of the black family, and that is why they killed him, and Malcolm X: at the end of their lives they understood that we were the Israelites.

The report on the black family showed about twenty percent of black families with one parent, the Watts riots broke out in 1965, and a whole battery of anti-poverty programs followed, Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society, built for the single mother instead of the husband and wife in the same house. They incentivized single motherhood, and that was strategic, to keep black men out of the house. But it is a punishment from God; we caused this on ourselves. We as Israelites allowed them to infect us, and Satan came in the garden the same way: he came at Eve. Sixty years later, eighty percent of black children are raised without two parents, and the result is weak, effeminate, angry men and women who can’t be told anything. Order in the house, with Christ at the head of the man, is what we have to restore to move our nation forward.

Marriage is work. Raising children is work. Getting to the kingdom is work. “And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws.” The root of an ordinance is order: men give order in families and in nations, just as the father represents the law in the house.

“And shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk.” The father, as the head of the family, shows them how to walk: when this happens in your life, you do this. When a son goes to his first job and may be one of the only blacks or Hispanics there, a father knows what to tell him, because he and the older generation have been through worse. Son, don’t give them all your personal information. Keep it light-hearted, talk about the weather, be nice, be respectable. But at the end of the day you are not going out drinking with them; you go home to your Israelite wife. Black men in this society are not armed with that, and that is what they took away from us. If we don’t walk in God’s laws, you get the sick black community out there: the worst obesity rate on earth, the worst STD rate, the worst education, high school dropouts, the school-to-prison pipeline.

“And the work that they must do.” You think you are going to get to the kingdom without doing anything? You’re a nut job. A man can believe he could be a veterinarian and sit back and hope for it, and he never becomes one because he did none of the work: the classes, the courses, the labs. It takes work to get to the end goal. The highway of the upright leads to the kingdom, and despite all the evil black folks have been through all these years, we still have to do the work. That is why Christianity is sick: a sorcery, a witch’s brew, a concoction of confusion.

Other nations help each other. Jewish families live together until thirty or thirty-five and move out with five or six hundred thousand dollars saved; the Chinese, Japanese and others do the same. Among us there is a stigma, pushed by many single mothers, that at eighteen you have to get out of the house, when a young man could contribute to the house, save, buy a car outright and put money down on a house. We are trying to live like Caucasians without their four-hundred-year head start. We must gather together, in health and in group economics.

“Gather yourselves together.” First and foremost, that is the Israelites gathering with the scriptures and learning how to walk on the pathway of the upright. “Yea, gather together”: Zephaniah repeats himself, because gathering together is more than the scriptures. It is group economics and building a government on earth, order and structure. The land being developed is just the beginning, and none of us should be shocked when we all get in shape, get our cars paid off and pay off our houses.

The CPAs, accountants, doctors, lawyers, veterinarians, carpenters and tile workers among us have a duty to instill it in our children and show them how they did it. We are building a nation. If a brother in the body can’t even fix his car while twelve of you have cars that run fine and you shut your mouth and do nothing, you are weak. The Israelites are supposed to stand together and are commanded to help each other. Every school should have mechanics, carpenters, plumbers and electricians helping the body, and someone teaching our people about credit, so that we put thousands of dollars a year back in our own pockets. That is part of us getting our Zephaniah 2:1.

This is the way Jesus the Christ thought, and Christ was no weak, effeminate black man. He was a strong, powerful man, and an upright man.

“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory”: that is what you see today, competing with the Joneses, she got that so I want that, dumb sisters out there competing over purses and outfits. “But in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” If I esteem you better than myself, then within my power I have to either help you come up with solutions or help to provide the solution.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” That does not mean just looking at a brother and saying, yep, he’s struggling like hell. Look means action, damn it.
“Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus.” That is the mind we had as a people at one point.

precepts.why:
We have to bear one another’s burdens; this is how we are going to rise. Zephaniah told us to gather together, and when you gather, you collect: we are gathering a nation and rising up. At the center of our walk on the highway of the upright is the nuclear family. From the strong father in the house comes the right way to eat, which destroys obesity, and the teaching a young man needs to deal with what he will face on his job and in society. Women can’t teach our men that. And the sister in the house balances the man: the son learns strength, structure and law from his father, and empathy from his mother. It is not a woman bash by any means.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” We just read about the mind of Christ: in lowliness of mind, esteem one another better, look on the things of the other brothers and sisters. We had that once. Black people used to speak to each other when we passed, because we had a common struggle, and brothers stood together against oppression. Now we have fallen apart.

sense.text:
Economics must be in our mindset as we walk to build a nation, because on the road of keeping the commandments evil is going to come upon you: they take your job because you are black or Hispanic or your last name is interesting. Half of black folks have a credit score below 620 and are locked out of capital. Racism and police brutality are real, and we obsess about them because we are going through them; add to that being unhealthy, a single-parent household with no law in the house, and now bad credit. Esau has law in his house: the grandfather passes the torch, the hard lessons and the wealth down, and that is why they had the head start. We are behind in everything, so it is of the utmost importance that we fix the marriage first, the nucleus.

“For wisdom is a defence”: generational wisdom passed from father to son, grandfather to son, son to son. “And money is a defence.” A brother with a good job who got divorced and is paying that money out does not have the defense he would have if he were married in proper order, where that money could do more. We have to set this up in our nation and take back our nation, and we are doing that slowly but surely.

“But the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.” In order to have it, you have to be taught it. That is why they are trying to stop us from teaching that we are the Israelites, the twelve tribes of Israel: we have been scattered, and we lost our nationality, our heritage and our commandments. The father in the house teaches health, teaches economics, and first and foremost teaches God’s commandments, his Sabbaths, his holy days, his dress code and his dietary laws. That is how we raise a generation that keeps no Christmas, no Easter bunny and no tooth fairy, and break the cycle.

Health is taught in the household too: when a father lays down the law, you’re not eating that; this is how we eat in my house. Nearly half of black adults are obese and about eight in ten black women are obese or overweight, and that was not so when there was a father and mother in the house. A sister not even in the truth lost a hundred and twenty pounds in her seventies; if she can do it, the brothers damn sure can. We have an enemy God put against us to correct us for our sin, but we have to fix the things we can control. God says we are above all people, so why can we not do what we have a concrete example of other nations doing for decades? The Amish come together and build a house for a newly married couple with no mortgage attached. We have the knowledge, the builders, the plumbers and the concrete men, and we can do this too, at a higher level.

“There is also another thing; A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things.” This place we live in now is not full of all good things. The city on the broad field is the kingdom, and it takes work in faith, demonstrated by our actions, to get there.

“The entrance thereof is narrow”: to get to that place full of good things you have to go through a narrow entrance, “and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water: And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.”

That is the title of the class: the highway of the upright, an Israelite’s strait journey. We are going to have to go through all these things in this captivity. This is our journey, and each one of us has to walk the strait path individually.

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance”: this is the kingdom of heaven. If you think God is not going to make our ways challenging, you are wrong. But what waits for us is that everything goes away, the sighing and the sorrow.

precepts.why:
Isaiah said what waits for us in that inheritance. You want all the stress to stop? We have to gather together as a nation and make it easier to build and help each other when the tough times come, losing your job because of your last name: fix our credit scores, fix our health, learn group economics and work together in the trades.

“And the ransomed of the Lord shall return”: that is what is happening. We were ransomed out to the nations, but we are returning, gathering together like Zephaniah 2 said. “And come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads.” We are not there yet, brothers and sisters, but we are going to Zion, through that strait gate to the broad field with the city.

“They shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.” We are going to be happy and full of gladness. The stress that comes from the bills and all of it is going to flee away and leave.
